steps: Stop the server, if it's running.
copy the whole cluster data directory and any tablespaces to a temporary location
Remove all existing files and subdirectories under the cluster data directory
If you're restoring a full backup, you can restore the database files directly into the target directories
If you're restoring an incremental backup
Remove any files present in pg_wal/
If you have unarchived WAL segment files that you saved in step 2, copy them into pg_wal/
Set recovery configuration settings in postgresql.conf
Start the server. The server will go into recovery mode

before: Use compressed dumps. You can use your favorite compression program
after: The split command allows you to split the output into smaller files

text: if you are using a customized template1, you must create the empty database from template0

b: The dumps produced by pg_dump are relative to template0

text: This option must be used with caution: if WAL archiving is not monitored correctly then the backup might not include all of the WAL files
If the file system containing pg_wal/ fills up, PostgreSQL will do a PANIC shutdown
The database server must be shut down in order to get a usable backup

a: GNU tar versions 1.16 and later exit with 1

text: Cluster-wide data can be dumped alone using the pg_dumpall --globals-only option
you can use the warning options --warning=no-file-changed --warning=no-file-removed
The backup label file includes the label string you gave to pg_backup_start
